item.description: The UuidStorage._lookup_path method raises KeyError: 'uuid' when trying to access cached external files. The issue occurs when checking if a location.path exists in self._external_files, but the dictionary doesn't contain the expected keys due to improper key construction or caching issues.
item.contract: When a UUID-based external location is accessed, the storage system should properly resolve the file path either from the cache or by generating a new UUID. The lookup mechanism should handle cases where UUIDs are not found in the cache gracefully and avoid KeyError exceptions.
item.acceptance: Tests that previously failed with KeyError: 'uuid' should pass, particularly tests in tests/external/storage/test_uuid.py and tests/external/test_formats.py

item.description: The External class fails with AttributeError: 'bytes' object has no attribute 'items' when processing encoded data. This happens because the code assumes data is a dictionary when it's actually bytes, likely during encoding/decoding operations in external storage handling.
item.contract: The External class should correctly handle various data types including bytes when processing external storage operations. The data handling should not assume dictionary structure for all data types.
item.acceptance: Tests in tests/test_encoding.py that previously failed with AttributeError: 'bytes' object has no attribute 'items' should pass

item.description: The formatting functionality fails with AssertionError in test_black_formatting_error and test_no_black tests. This indicates that the formatting validation logic doesn't properly handle edge cases or error conditions in the formatting process.
item.contract: The formatting system should properly validate and handle formatting operations, including when black is not available or when formatting fails. It should provide appropriate error messages and fallback behavior rather than raising AssertionErrors.
item.acceptance: Tests in tests/test_formatting.py that previously failed with AssertionError should pass
